subject.title: [Feature]: [Feature Request] 按用户维度统计 Token 使用量

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class user-bucketed token usage accounting in core, and what principal should define the user for attribution, authorization, retention, and quota/billing views?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior changes identity, privacy, storage, Gateway RPC, Dashboard, `/usage`, and quota/billing semantics in a project documented around a trusted single-operator Gateway boundary.

options.title: Design Core Identity Accounting
options.body: Define the user principal, authorized readers, storage schema, aggregation RPCs, Dashboard and `/usage` behavior, retention, and redaction rules before implementation.

options.title: Use External Reporting First
options.body: Keep core usage as session, agent, channel, model, and provider aggregates while front layers or plugins map authenticated users to sessions for billing reports.

options.title: Defer Until Principal Work Lands
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until the multi-token identity and usage-ledger decisions are settled.

recommendation.title: Design Core Identity Accounting
recommendation.body: Define the user principal, authorized readers, storage schema, aggregation RPCs, Dashboard and `/usage` behavior, retention, and redaction rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest usage-cost surface history and can route the identity/security half to Gateway auth owners.
